newsitem.title: USA: Iomega plans low-cost miniature data storage device.
newsitem.headline: Iomega plans low-cost miniature data storage device.

text.p: Iomega Corp. said Thursday it plans to develop a technology that can save and transfer data between a variety of handheld consumer electronic devices.
The data storage device, to be known as "n-hand," could be used in digital cameras, computer game devices, cellular phones and handheld personal computers known as digital assistants.
"Our n-hand technology ... has the potential to change the way consumers use portable electronic devices," Kim Edwards, Iomega's president and chief executive, said in a statement.
For example, a reporter in the field could snap a picture and send the image over a cell phone to an office computer for processing.

A digital camera could store from 70 to 80 images on a single $10 n-hand disk, Iomega said. Currently, consumers pay hundreds of dollars for a flash memory card capable of holding the same number of images, it noted.

The n-hand disks are expected to be priced at less than $10 for a 20-megabyte disk, and could be available by the second half of 1997. Iomega said the n-hand disks are about half the size of a business card.
Shares of the company were up $1.375 to $25.375 in late afternoon trading on Thursday on the Nasdaq. On Friday, Iomega's stock will begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
